citations.K64.1: The Tabular List gives code K64.1 the inclusion term 'Hemorrhoids (bleeding) that prolapse with straining, but retract spontaneously', and the Alphabetic Index carries the same words at 'Hemorrhoids, 2nd degree'. ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.A.11: inclusion terms are the conditions for which that code is to be used. Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. Here the gastroenterologist's assessment is 'bleeding internal hemorrhoids that prolapse with straining but retract spontaneously', which is the inclusion term almost word for word, so the code for second degree hemorrhoids is assigned although the note names no degree.

coder_notes: Counter-case: the more specific code is the supported one. The codes for hemorrhoids without mention of degree (K64.8 for internal or prolapsed hemorrhoids, K64.9) apply when the degree is neither named nor described; here the provider's own diagnostic statement describes it in the words of the classification. This differs from deriving a detail from examination findings or test values: the coder interprets nothing, because the statement and the inclusion term are the same words. By the inclusion terms of K64.0 and K64.2, first degree hemorrhoids do not prolapse outside the anal canal and third degree hemorrhoids need manual replacement. The bleeding is named in the inclusion term and is a routine sign of hemorrhoids, so no code for hemorrhage of the anus and rectum is added (Section I.B.5). There is no thrombosis, no external hemorrhoid and no skin tag. The blood count is normal. Constipation is not documented.
